strengths: Principled and novel formulation: Bridging classical linear dynamical system theory (specifically extended observability subspaces and P-equivalence) with modern State Space Models (SSMs) on the infinite-dimensional Grassmannian provides a fresh and theoretically grounded perspective on regularizing continual learners.

Computational elegance: By leveraging the diagonal structure of the transition matrix A in structured SSMs (e.g., S4D, Vim), the authors show how to bypass the standard O(n^3) Bartels-Stewart Sylvester solver and arrive at an exact O(n^2) element-wise formulation, making infinite-horizon regularization practical.

Consistent empirical gains: Inf-SSM and Inf-SSM+ consistently outperform traditional regularization and distillation baselines (EwC, SI, MAS, LwF) on multiple benchmarks (ImageNet-R, CIFAR-100, Caltech-256) by significantly reducing the forgetting measure (FM) and maintaining higher average accuracy.

Modularity and plug-and-play capability: The method is successfully combined with replay-based approaches (ER, LUCIR, X-DER) and prompt-based approaches (L2P-R), demonstrating its versatility beyond strictly exemplar-free setups.
weaknesses: Comparison primarily against older foundational baselines: In the core experiments (Tables 1, 4, and 5), the comparison is limited to foundational regularizers (EwC, SI, MAS, LwF). Modern exemplar-free class-incremental learning (EFCIL) approaches (such as FeTrIL, SSRE, or LDC) and recent Mamba-tailored CL methods mentioned in related work (e.g., Mamba-CL, Mamba-FSCIL) are not directly compared empirically.

Gap between rigorous theory and heuristic approximations in S6/Vim: Selective SSMs have input-dependent, time-varying parameters. To make the theoretical formulation tractable, the authors apply aggressive heuristic approximations—averaging across the outer dimension and using a noisy rank-1 trace approximation in Eq. (38) with ad-hoc threshold checks (Appendix D.5). This weakens the rigorous geometric guarantees of the original Grassmannian formulation.

Evaluation limited to a single architecture: Experiments are conducted exclusively on Vim-Small. Evaluating across different model scales or other SSM variants (e.g., VMamba, or 1D sequential/language tasks where Mamba is predominantly adopted) would significantly strengthen the empirical claims.

strengths: Novel and principled formulation: Leveraging the extended observability subspace and the geometry of the infinite-dimensional Grassmannian to respect P-equivalence (similarity transform invariance) in SSMs is a creative, theoretically grounded approach to continual learning.

Computational elegance: By taking advantage of the diagonal structure of the state transition matrix in modern structured SSMs (e.g., S4D, Vim), the authors reduce the complexity of solving the continuous-time/discrete Sylvester equation from cubic O(n^3) to quadratic O(n^2), rendering the infinite-horizon metric computationally feasible.

Comprehensive empirical verification: The proposed method achieves substantial reductions in catastrophic forgetting and improvements in accuracy across multiple benchmarks (ImageNet-R, CIFAR-100, Caltech-256) in both 5-task and 10-task settings.

Modularity and versatility: The paper demonstrates that Inf-SSM is complementary to diverse continual learning paradigms, showing consistent gains when integrated with replay-based methods (ER, LUCIR, X-DER) and prompt-based approaches (L2P-R).
weaknesses: Heuristic bridging from LTI theory to Selective SSMs (S6): The core theoretical foundation (extended observability and infinite Grassmannian invariance) strictly holds for Linear Time-Invariant (LTI) systems. In Vision Mamba / S6, parameters are dynamically generated and input-dependent. The averaging across outer dimensions and heuristic soft-normalization to force Schur stability weaken the theoretical purity of the infinite-horizon observability claim.

Handling of system controllability (matrix B): The extended observability matrix only captures (A, C) pairs and ignores B. Adding an ad-hoc Euclidean/Frobenius penalty for B in Inf-SSM+ breaks the P-equivalence orbit invariance that motivated the formulation in the first place, as noted in the limitations.

Baseline comparisons: Experimental comparisons in the main text are primarily restricted to foundational CL regularizers from 2017–2018 (EWC, SI, MAS, LwF). Direct quantitative comparisons against recent specialized SSM continual learning methods discussed in the related work (e.g., Mamba-CL, MambaCL) or modern exemplar-free techniques (e.g., SSRE, LDC, EFC) are missing.

Implementation and memory overhead: As discussed in Appendix E, extracting intermediate state representations disrupts the fused hardware-optimized CUDA scan kernels ('scan-breaking'), which increases runtime and VRAM footprint during training.

strengths: Principled motivation: Addressing continual learning in State-Space Models (SSMs) by considering system-theoretic invariance (P-equivalence) and observability subspaces is an original and mathematically elegant perspective.

Computational optimization: Exploiting the diagonal structure of structured SSMs (e.g., S4D/Mamba) to simplify the Sylvester equation from O(n^3) to an O(n^2) Hadamard-based formulation is an insightful and practical derivation.

Extensive empirical validation: The paper tests the approach across multiple benchmarks (ImageNet-R, CIFAR-100, Caltech-256), under both exemplar-free settings and integrated with replay-based (ER, LUCIR, X-DER) and prompt-based (L2P) continual learning paradigms.
weaknesses: Theoretical mismatch with Selective SSMs (S6): The theoretical foundation of extended observability and the Sylvester equation fundamentally assumes Linear Time-Invariant (LTI) systems. However, modern vision SSMs like Vision Mamba (Vim) rely on Selective SSMs (S6), where parameters (B, C, and the step size delta) are dynamic, time-varying, and input-dependent. The proposed workaround—averaging states across the outer dimension and applying soft-normalization (Section 3.4 and Appendix D.3)—is largely heuristic and severs the rigorous mathematical connection to the infinite Grassmannian observability framework.

Ad-hoc distance approximation: In Appendix D.5, the authors note that the observability Gramians are rank-deficient and ill-conditioned, leading them to substitute the exact Grassmannian chordal distance with a rank-1 trace approximation and an empirical threshold check (cos theta = 0 if |A - A'| <= epsilon and |C - C'| <= epsilon). This compromises the geometric rigor and theoretical guarantees claimed in the main text.

Practical training overhead and scan-breaking: As acknowledged in Appendix E, extracting intermediate time-varying states requires breaking the optimized hardware-fused selective scan CUDA kernels and materializing hidden states in memory. This introduces non-trivial training time and VRAM overhead, which limits the practical utility of the method in large-scale sequential learning settings.

Baseline scope: The primary comparisons in the main tables are against classical foundational regularizers (EwC, SI, MAS, LwF) adapted to SSM parameters. Modern SOTA exemplar-free class-incremental learning baselines (e.g., SSRE, FeTrIL, RanPAC) are only mentioned in the related work and not empirically compared.

strengths: Principled and novel formulation: The paper introduces a well-motivated control-theoretic approach to continual learning in State Space Models (SSMs). By formalizing the P-equivalence invariance of SSMs and regularizing the extended observability subspace on the infinite Grassmannian, it addresses catastrophic forgetting through the intrinsic geometry of the state space rather than treating SSM parameters as generic weights.

Computational efficiency: The authors effectively exploit the diagonal structure of modern structured SSMs (e.g., S4D, Vim) to solve the infinite-horizon Sylvester equation in closed-form $O(n^2)$ entry-wise operations instead of standard $O(n^3)$ solvers, making distance computation on an infinite Grassmannian practical during training.

Broad empirical gains and versatility: Extensive experiments across multiple benchmarks (ImageNet-R, CIFAR-100, Caltech-256) and task lengths (5 and 10 tasks) demonstrate consistent gains. Inf-SSM serves both as a competitive standalone exemplar-free method (outperforming EWC, SI, MAS, LwF, UCL) and as a plug-and-play regularizer that improves replay-based and hybrid methods (ER, LUCIR, X-DER, L2P-R, CLFD).

Thorough analysis and supplementary ablation: The manuscript provides insightful diagnostic analyses, including Centered Kernel Disparity (CKD) across layers, layer-wise ablation studies, and evaluation on different model scales (Vim-tiny and Vim-small).
weaknesses: Gap between theoretical derivation and practical approximation: While the main paper presents the exact chordal distance on $Gr(n, \infty)$ via Gramian inverses (Eq. 11–14), Appendix D.5 reveals that in practice, because $O$ is rank-deficient and ill-conditioned, a rank-1 approximation and trace ratio (Eq. 33) is used instead to ensure numerical stability. The main text should explicitly discuss this rank-1 relaxation and its theoretical fidelity rather than relegating it to the appendix.

Heuristic channel collapsing for S6/Mamba: For time-varying architectures where parameters vary across sequence length and outer feature channels, the method averages over the outer dimension $o$ to obtain manageable matrices. While variance preservation is reported in Table 5, averaging channels collapses inter-channel dynamical interactions, which weakens the formal representation invariance guarantees for the full multi-channel model.

Implementation and memory overhead ('scan-breaking'): Because intermediate state dynamics ($A, C$) in selective SSMs are computed inside highly optimized fused CUDA kernels, extracting them outside the kernel incurs a 'scan-breaking' memory and runtime penalty during backpropagation, as acknowledged in Appendix E.

Hyperparameter variance: Across different datasets and baseline integrations (Tables 12–19), the regularization coefficient $\lambda$ varies drastically across multiple orders of magnitude (from $10^0$ up to $2.5 \times 10^6$). Providing guidance or a normalized scale for $\lambda$ would improve practical usability.

strengths: Novel and elegant theoretical foundation: To the best of knowledge, this is the first work to address continual learning in State-Space Models (SSMs) by explicitly exploiting their system-theoretic geometry. Formulating state-space preservation via the P-equivalence invariance of the extended observability subspace on the infinite Grassmannian is both mathematically sound and original.

Efficient formulation tailored to modern SSMs: The authors show that computing distances on the infinite Grassmannian reduces to solving a discrete Sylvester equation. By exploiting the diagonal structure of transition matrix A in architectures such as S4D, Mamba, and Vision Mamba, they derive an O(n^2) element-wise closed-form solution, bypassing standard O(n^3) Bartels-Stewart solvers and drastically reducing computational overhead.

Strong and consistent empirical improvements: The proposed Inf-SSM demonstrates notable gains across three benchmarks (ImageNet-R, CIFAR-100, Caltech-256) in both 5-task and 10-task settings. As a standalone exemplar-free method, it outperforms standard regularization baselines (EWC, SI, MAS, LwF, UCL). When integrated with replay, hybrid, and prompt-based baselines (ER, LUCIR, X-DER, L2P-R, CLFD), it consistently improves final average accuracy (AA) and lowers the forgetting measure (FM).

Thorough experimental ablations and appendix: The supplementary material provides proofs, an analysis of state drift across layers using Centered Kernel Disparity (CKD), latency benchmarks, explorations on regularizing the input matrix B (Inf-SSM+), and evaluations on Vim-tiny.
weaknesses: Heuristic gap between theory and practical instantiation in S6/Vim: The foundational theory is developed for Linear Time-Invariant (LTI) systems with exact chordal distance. In contrast, modern selective SSMs (S6 in Vim) have dynamic, position-dependent, and multi-channel states. To make computation tractable, the authors apply several heuristic approximations: averaging across the channel dimension o, applying soft-normalization for Schur stability, and adopting a rank-1 trace approximation for the principal angle (Eq. 33). While empirically justified, the main text understates the gap between the clean theoretical Grassmannian formulation and these practical approximations.

Neglect of the controllability/input matrix B: The extended observability subspace only involves the pair (A, C), inherently omitting input projection B. While Appendix H.4 explores adding an L2 regularizer on B (Inf-SSM+) and finds minimal difference, a full input-output realization in classical linear system theory requires both observability and reachability/controllability (e.g., Hankel singular values). A more rigorous theoretical discussion clarifying why regularizing observability alone is sufficient in practice would enhance the paper.

Evaluation scope limited to Vision Mamba (Vim): The empirical validation is conducted strictly on Vim-small and Vim-tiny. Validating on other visual SSM backbones (e.g., VMamba with 2D selective scan) or 1D sequence/NLP Mamba tasks would significantly strengthen the claim of broad applicability across the SSM architecture family.

Training memory and runtime trade-offs: As acknowledged in Appendix E, extracting intermediate states (A, B, C) breaks the hardware-efficient fused scan kernel of Mamba, requiring states to be materialized and retained outside the kernel. The authors report loss computation latency in Table 3, but a complete measurement of end-to-end training epoch time and peak VRAM overhead during actual backpropagation compared to standard baselines is missing from the main text.

strengths: Principled and novel formulation: Addressing catastrophic forgetting in State-Space Models (SSMs) through the lens of system representation invariance (P-equivalence) and the infinite-dimensional Grassmannian of observability subspaces is conceptually sound, elegant, and well-motivated from dynamical systems theory.

Computational efficiency: The authors effectively exploit the diagonal parameterization common in modern SSMs (e.g., S4D, Mamba, Vim) to reduce the Sylvester equation resolution from an expensive O(n^3) Bartels-Stewart solver to an efficient O(n^2) Hadamard formulation.

Consistent and strong empirical gains: Integrating Inf-SSM into diverse continual learning baselines (replay, hybrid, prompt-based, frequency-based) consistently reduces forgetting (FM) and improves final accuracy (AA) across multiple benchmarks (ImageNet-R, CIFAR-100, Caltech-256) and across model scales (Vim-small and Vim-tiny).

Exemplar-free compatibility: The method operates without requiring stored exemplars or memory buffers from past tasks, making it practical for privacy-sensitive and storage-constrained lifelong learning scenarios.
weaknesses: Theoretical gap between LTI theory and selective SSMs: The mathematical foundation relies on Linear Time-Invariant (LTI) dynamics to define the infinite-horizon observability matrix O_\infty(A, C). However, Vision Mamba (S6) operates with input-dependent, time-varying dynamics across sequence tokens. Treating each token index independently as an infinite trajectory and averaging across channel dimensions are practical heuristics that dilute the formal guarantees of the infinite Grassmannian distance.

Practical training overhead and fused scan breakage: In selective SSM architectures like Mamba/Vim, intermediate states (A, B, C) are generated dynamically within fused hardware-aware selective scan CUDA kernels. As acknowledged in the appendix, extracting these matrices requires materializing states outside the kernel, introducing memory and runtime overhead during continual training.

Ad-hoc rank-1 approximation for Grassmannian distance: Due to numerical ill-conditioning of the Gram matrices in practice, the authors substitute the exact chordal distance with a simplified rank-1 trace ratio (Eq. 33). While empirically justified via Monte Carlo correlation, this departs from the true Grassmannian metric structure.

Evaluation scope limited primarily to Vim backbones: Although the theoretical motivation applies broadly to structured SSMs, all visual continual learning experiments are conducted exclusively on Vision Mamba (Vim-small and Vim-tiny), without validation on other sequence SSMs (e.g., 2D-selective VMamba or 1D sequential benchmarks).
